name: Art Institute of Chicago
tagline: Encyclopedic. Includes Nighthawks, La Grande Jatte. Allow a full day.
description: One of the largest encyclopedic art museums in the United States. Holdings include Impressionist masterpieces (Monet, Renoir, Caillebotte), American icons (Hopper's Nighthawks, Wood's American Gothic), and a Modern Wing designed by Renzo Piano.
review_long:
The Art Institute is one of three or four museums in the country you can fairly call encyclopedic. Its painting wing alone houses the largest Impressionist collection outside Paris — Monet's Haystacks, Renoir's Two Sisters, the Caillebottes — and its modern wing, designed by Renzo Piano in 2009, exhibits Hopper, Pollock, O'Keeffe, and Picasso's The Old Guitarist in rooms that are themselves worth the visit.

Plan a full day. The Thorne Miniature Rooms, often overlooked, are on the lower level and worth an hour on their own.

tips.text: Illinois residents get free admission Thursday evenings 5–8 PM.
Skip Saturdays — try Tuesday or Wednesday instead.
